name: Green-veg & chicken glass-noodle stir-fry

source.author: Hebrew recipe (screenshot)
source.notes: Analyzed from a pasted Hebrew ingredient list. Method not shown (assumed standard stir-fry: sear chicken, stir-fry veg, add noodles + sauce). No ginger, sweetener, or cornstarch/thickener was listed — if the full recipe includes one, macros shift slightly. Veg weights are given; soy/oil retention and servings estimated. Bigger, greener sibling of chicken_stir_fry.

steps: Sear the chicken strips until cooked; set aside.
Stir-fry garlic + chili, then the green beans, zucchini, broccoli until crisp-tender.
Add the soaked glass noodles, both soy sauces and sesame oil; toss.
Fold in the spinach and green onion until just wilted; return the chicken and combine.

him.verdict: Nutritionally one of the best mains here — 44 g protein/serving (~9.2 g protein per 100 kcal), a huge load of green veg, ~5 g fiber/serving (32 g across the batch), plus real folate/iron/vitamin C. The single thing dragging it from a 9 to a 7 is SODIUM: 8 tbsp of soy total (~1,133 mg/serving — roughly half a day's limit in one plate). Fat is moderate (~14 g from 3–4 tbsp olive + sesame oil); glass noodles are refined but well-balanced by all the veg.
flags: folate + iron + vitamin C from spinach/broccoli
VERY high sodium (~1,133 mg/serving, 8 tbsp soy)
suggested_mods: Use low-sodium soy and cut the total soy to ~4–5 tbsp — this is the one real fix; it nearly halves the sodium
Trim frying oil toward 2 tbsp to shave fat
Otherwise excellent as-is — one of the highest-veg, highest-fiber mains in the library

her_preconception.verdict: Excellent for her — arguably the best preconception main analyzed. Spinach + broccoli + green beans stack up serious FOLATE (~80 mcg DFE/serving after cooking, the #1 preconception nutrient), IRON (~3.2 mg) that's naturally paired with the dish's own vitamin C (~42 mg) for better absorption, plus lean protein + choline. Fully cooked, no safety flags. Only caveat: the sodium — ease it with low-sodium soy.
prenatal_highlights: high folate from spinach + broccoli + green beans (top preconception nutrient)
iron (~3.2 mg) paired with the dish's own vitamin C (~42 mg) for absorption
lean protein + choline; broad green-veg micros

safety_advisories.note: High sodium (~1,133 mg/serving from 8 tbsp soy) — worth easing in pregnancy.
safety_advisories.swap: low-sodium soy, cut total soy to 4–5 tbsp

suggested_mods: This is a keeper for her preconception nutrients — just dial down the soy
Serve promptly so the folate-rich greens aren't overcooked/held too long

cooking_guide: Prep everything before you start. Soak the glass noodles in warm water until pliable, drain, and snip shorter.
Blanch or steam the broccoli and green beans ~2 min (they're denser than the rest), then shock in cold water to keep them bright green and crisp.
Pat the chicken dry and sear in a hot wok in a single layer until just cooked; remove and set aside.
Stir-fry the garlic and chili briefly, then the zucchini and the blanched greens over high heat 2-3 min — crisp-tender, not soft.
Add the noodles with both soy sauces and the sesame oil and toss to coat.
Return the chicken, then fold in the spinach and green onion at the very end — spinach wilts in seconds, and overcooking dulls it and loses folate.
Serve promptly. Tip: use low-sodium soy and taste before adding more — 8 tbsp of soy is very salty.
